decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up lift and gradual downward gripper orientation; basket is in right workspace.
Approach above basket while increasing downward tilt, keeping right elbow configuration continuous.
Align right gripper vertically above the rear egg; maintain clearance before descending.
Lower open fingers cautiously toward rear egg; wrist view will refine lateral alignment.
Center on rear-right egg using wrist view and descend another 3.5 cm with fingers open.
Back away slightly from basket rim, center shifted egg, and close fingers for first grasp; contact limited prior descent.
Lift first egg vertically with closed gripper and verify retention before transfer.
Carry retained egg above holder's right-rear cup, tilting inward while keeping the right wrist in right workspace.
Lid unexpectedly closed during transfer. Move held egg clear and prepare left arm to reopen holder; retention view is occluded.
Egg slipped onto table left of holder. Free right gripper and approach the closed lid from its front to reopen it.
Rotate free right gripper to a vertical pinch and move toward the lid's front lip with clearance.
Continue front-lip approach, keeping the right arm on its side and gradually turning fingers vertical.
Lower vertical jaws in front of the lid edge, leaving clearance before attempting to pinch and lift the lip.
Replan after rejected rotation: retain current nearly horizontal approach orientation and lower in small increments toward lid lip.
Lower jaw appears blocked by lid top. Retract in front of holder, then lower to straddle its lip rather than press it.
Recover from wrist continuity limit by lifting and moving outward with a modest reverse roll; reapproach lid from an accessible angle.
Reposition right arm for a diagonal lid-edge approach; begin left-arm approach to the egg on the left table.
Use much smaller right wrist yaw increments after continuity rejection; approach dropped egg with left arm.
Advance left above dropped egg and continue right-arm side approach to reopen lid, with both arms separated.
Align left fingers above the loose egg and bring right vertical jaws to the holder's right edge for lid reopening.
Replan right approach with smaller increments and downward inclination for elbow clearance; left aligns over loose egg.
Lower left fingers around loose egg; incline right jaws toward lid edge with minimal translation to avoid pressing the lid top.
Close left gripper on loose egg; retract right fingertips clear of lid edge before lowering to catch its lip.
Lift retained loose egg with left arm. Probe a small right-side lid pinch; retention and lid engagement remain visually uncertain.
Keep left egg secure. Raise right wrist and incline fingers downward to improve elbow clearance while approaching the lid side.
Attempt a shallow pinch of the lid's right-front overhang while holding the recovered egg clear with the left arm.
Test lid-edge engagement by lifting along a shallow opening arc; keep recovered egg stationary and closed.
First pinch did not lift lid. Reopen and align a little farther onto the right lip, just above its surface.
Withdraw from the lid surface and lower closed tips outside its side edge to try lifting underneath the overhang.
Slide closed tips gently toward the underside of the lid's right-front edge, then inspect contact.
Clear basket-side interference by moving toward the holder front; lower closed tips below the lid surface outside the box.
Wrist lowering is obstructed. Increase downward finger inclination while raising the wrist, to reach under the lid edge without lowering the elbow.
Probe just beneath the right-front lip using closed fingertips, then test a small upward lift; left egg remains held clear.
Withdraw from obstructed side approach and reposition in front of holder with a downward-angled wrist, avoiding basket interference.
Move right wrist toward the front-right lid corner with open angled jaws, maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Align angled jaws with the front lid lip, lowering with the wrist above the holder and the lower jaw outside its front wall.
Close on the front lip from the current straddling position and test a short upward lift.
Test the front-lip pinch along an upward opening arc, keeping left egg stationary.
Lid appears slightly separated at its edge. Continue the closed-gripper opening arc gradually and inspect whether the hinge follows.
Lid is visibly opening. Follow its hinge arc farther back while maintaining the pinch and keeping the recovered egg clear.
Continue opening the lid toward upright using a slower hinge arc; left arm keeps its egg clear.
Replan after continuity rejection: pivot the right wrist back around its lid contact to recover joint margin without pulling the lid shut.
Advance lid a little farther toward upright using small increments after recovering wrist joint margin.
Ease the lid beyond upright while carrying the recovered egg toward the holder's left side, keeping both grippers closed.
Separate the wrists by moving the left egg toward the holder front, while gently pushing the lid farther back with the right fingertips.
Withdraw right arm from the open lid and lower the left-held egg toward the front-left cup.
Egg slipped beside holder; reopen left fingers and reapproach it lower. Right arm returns to a downward basket grasp orientation, clear of the now-open lid.
Lower left fingers around the loose egg, away from the holder wall. Align right open fingers over the front basket egg.
Narrow open jaws to avoid the holder and basket walls, align both eggs under the fingertips, and descend gently.
Close right fingers around the centered basket egg. Withdraw left wrist from holder collision before changing its grasp direction.
Test right egg retention with a small lift; turn left jaws parallel to holder wall to avoid collision on the next descent.
Right grasp missed above the egg; reopen and descend deeper at its new front position. Lower left jaws parallel to holder wall around the loose egg.
Use wrist views to recenter each egg between the fingers, then close both grippers without lifting yet.
Lift the right egg to verify retention. Left pinch was too shallow; reopen and lower around the loose egg's equator.
Carry the visibly retained right egg slowly toward the holder. Recenter left fingers above the loose egg after it rolled forward.
Continue slow right-egg transfer above the holder's front-right cup. Left egg rolled forward; withdraw left hand clear before recovering it.
Align the retained right egg over the front-right cup and lower slowly. Move left gripper above the loose egg near the table front.
Seat and release the right egg in the front-right cup. Lower the left hand toward the loose egg, checking alignment before closing.
First egg is visibly seated; lift the open right gripper clear. Shift left fingers toward the loose egg's center without closing yet.
Close left fingers on the loose egg after the small alignment correction. Return right hand above the remaining basket eggs.
Left pinch was above the egg; reopen and descend to its sides. Approach the basket's right egg with the right fingers partially open.
Lift and untwist the obstructed left wrist. Center right fingertips over the remaining right basket egg and lower cautiously.
Narrow right fingers to clear the rim and grasp deeper around the egg. Finish untwisting left wrist and recenter over the loose egg.
Both eggs are offset from the pinch centers. Move left forward and down; reopen right and follow its egg toward the basket front before a deeper grasp.
Close left fingers after a small centering descent. Straighten right grasp vertically to reduce rim interference before closing again.
Both pinches remain above the eggs. Reopen and lower fingers to the egg equators, using small vertical increments.
Follow the eggs slightly toward the camera and close both pinches, narrowing before further descent to avoid rim and table contact.
Lift both closed grippers vertically to check egg retention before attempting another transfer.
Both eggs remained behind. Correct left tilt to vertical, shift right pinch toward the basket front, and descend open fingers deeper around each egg.
Center both visibly low eggs between the pads by moving toward the camera, then close without lifting.
Both eggs remain below the pinch pads. Reopen and lower vertically another small amount to grasp below their widest points.
Recenter left pinch on the egg behind its pads. Straighten right fingers and move wrist inside the basket rim to reduce contact obstruction.
Test left retention with a vertical lift. Angle the right fingers toward the front egg while bringing the wrist farther inside the basket to clear its rim.
